corrosion_narrative: The average mild steel corrosion rate was 0.5622 MPY against the target of within 3.0 MPY, and the average copper corrosion rate was 0.4506 MPY against the target of within 0.5 MPY. Status: Excellent. Corrosion control was Excellent because both metals remained below their target limits during the August reporting period. Both mild steel and copper corrosion decreased across the month, indicating inhibitor residual and operating chemistry kept corrosion protected.
corrosion_chart_comment: Corrosion decreased across the month and remained within target.
scale_narrative: Status: Acceptable. Traced Product averaged 65.57 ppm against the 100.00 ppm Controller Setpoint. A configured lower and upper control range was not available in SCC, so percent-in-range could not be calculated for this reporting month. Traced Product increased from about 32.6 ppm early in the month to 98.5 ppm later in the month, showing recovery toward the setpoint by month end. Conductivity also moved slightly lower during the month, so product and conductivity behavior should be reviewed together with field residuals before making feed-control changes.
scale_chart_comment: Traced Product increased toward the controller setpoint by the end of the month.
microbial_narrative: FRC data was not available in the field data for this reporting period and will be checked during the upcoming service visit. ORP did not show a strong spike response pattern during the month, but biocide relay activity was present, supporting an Acceptable microbial control status pending field residual confirmation. Copper corrosion remained within target, indicating no copper corrosion upset was observed during the reporting period.
orp_chart_comment: ORP response was not strong and should be verified with field FRC testing.
water_efficiency_narrative: Water efficiency was Acceptable. Conductivity averaged 957.58 uS/cm against the 1000.00 uS/cm Controller Setpoint. A configured lower and upper control range was not available in SCC, so percent-in-range could not be calculated for conductivity. Conductivity moved from about 964.5 uS/cm early in the month to 950.7 uS/cm later, indicating a slight decreasing pattern that should be reviewed against makeup, blowdown, dilution, or water-loss activity.
conductivity_chart_comment: Conductivity decreased slightly and remained below the controller setpoint average.
product_efficiency_narrative: Product efficiency needs continued monitoring because Traced Product averaged below the 100.00 ppm setpoint while increasing toward target later in the month. Polymer consumption rate averaged -10.6%, indicating the tagged-polymer signal was higher than the Traced Product signal and field residual confirmation is needed. Verify phosphate, silica, and product residuals during the next service visit before changing pump stroke or feed logic.
proactive_support_narrative: No service notes were recorded for the August reporting period. Recommended follow-up should focus on unresolved health-check items: verify Traced Product residual and fluorometer calibration as product recovers toward setpoint, review conductivity with makeup and blowdown behavior, check FRC and dip-slide CFU during the upcoming service visit, and verify phosphate and silica residuals against the polymer consumption trend.
closing_summary: Overall August performance for Synthomer showed Excellent corrosion control and Acceptable microbial and water-efficiency performance. The main follow-up is to confirm product residual recovery toward setpoint and validate field residuals because SCC did not provide lower and upper control limits for percent-in-range calculation. Continued review of conductivity, FRC, dip-slide CFU, phosphate, and silica residuals is recommended during the next service visit.
